> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

## Tips & gotchas

- Bleed the system extensively, potentially with a vacuum pump, as air removal can be difficult. [t1242]
- Wagoneer axles are 6-lug and match well to H233b width specifications. [t2278]
- Late 70s F150 D44s feature high pinions which can be beneficial but add width. [t2278]
- Look for a dedicated website resource specifically for first-gen SAS info. [t1277]
- [Partial] Plan on re-gearing the front axle unless buying a pre-swapped unit. [t1476]
- Consider long-travel radius arms to prevent binding issues common in Jeeps. [t1476]
- Drill and tap Chevy knuckles if a hi-steer setup is desired. [t1476]
- Use an inverted T steering setup with anti-roll bushings on top of tie rods and drag link ends to avoid hi-steer. [t1476]
- Consider leaf springs if you want the simplest route. [t1481]
- Coilovers provide a better long-term ride but may require more tuning. [t1481]
- If using a Dana 44, plan to upgrade axle shafts and ball joints for tires larger than 35 inches. [t1481]
- Consider running a subframe if installing a larger engine. [t1481]
- [Partial] Use chromoly axle shafts to handle stress from large tires and gearing. [t1481]
- Solid axles offer beefy steering components and true lockers. [t1471]
- [Partial] Provides more flex than an independent front suspension (IFS). [t1471]
- Allows for endless customization of height without being forced into a specific lift. [t1471]
- [Partial] Ensure right angles and proper setup for the best performance. [t1477]
- [Partial] Consider a coilover or 3-link suspension system to maximize flex. [t1477]
- [Partial] Buy the joints, DOM tubing, and pre-manufactured trackbars yourself to save money. [t1477]
- [Partial] Measure exact requirements to customize the setup for specific needs. [t1477]
- [Partial] Note: A body lift alone only allows 33-inch tires; it does not add significant ground clearance underneath without a solid axle. [t1477]
- Be aware that too much height raises the center of gravity. [t1477]
- [Partial] This is an alternative to a full 3-link or radius arm setup. [t1477]
- [Partial] Provides slightly more articulation than stock arms. [t1477]
- Preferred if not wheeling hard enough to justify expensive coilovers. [t1477]
- More predictable on the trail than a standard spring setup. [t1477]
- Essential safety piece for highway driving with a solid axle. [t1477]
- Helps mitigate the 'tight steering' feel common on highways. [t1477]
- [Partial] Crucial for highway stability and reducing vibration on a solid axle. [t1477]
- Part of the 'safety pieces' needed to make it road-worthy. [t1477]
- New Upper Control Arms (UCAs) are a good starting point for this upgrade. [t1477]
- [Partial] Helps handle the extra stress of a solid front axle. [t1477]
- Provides 'insane flex' and better offroad capability than stock IFS. [t1477]
- Part of the complete SAS conversion for serious rock crawling. [t1477]
- [Partial] Helps prevent excessive body roll when one end of the solid axle is in motion. [t1477]
- Considered a necessary safety piece for highway use. [t1477]
- [Partial] Use a D60 Kingpin setup for strength. [t1474]
- Select chromoly shafts to handle the increased load. [t1474]
- [Partial] The rear crossmember notch is necessary because increased lift causes the driveshaft to hit it, a common issue on WD21 Pathfinders as well. [t1474]
- [Partial] The front 3rd member is approximately 1/2" longer than the aesthetic alternative but functions well without ABS. [t1474]
- [Partial] The front axle sits on sway bar coilovers that carry the vehicle's weight until other components are fully integrated. [t1474]
- Trim fenders to accommodate wider tires while retaining as much of the factory shape as possible. [t1474]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Leaving the ABS box in place without hard tubing, leading to spongy pedals. [t1242]
- [Partial] Mounting front calipers on the wrong side so bleed nipples aren't at the top (specifically for Dana axles). [t1242]
- [Partial] Using a master cylinder with an M10 port that doesn't match the truck's M12 output. [t1242]
